title: The panes reply marks the scratch pane and the caller's own pane
body:
An agent calls the MCP tool `panes` to learn the workspace's panes. decade answers with a `decade_channel::Pane` per pane, in the shape of the socket's `panes` reply. A `Pane` has `name`, `client` and `shows`. The reply does not say which pane is the scratch pane, or which pane the calling agent runs in.

An agent in a decade workspace reported both gaps. It could not tell whether decade had recorded the scratch pane Jack marked, except by calling `scratch.open` and seeing whether it failed. It guessed its own pane from the `client: coax` entry, which fails once two panes run coax.

decade already gives each program it starts in a pane its pane name in `DECADE_PANE` (`Children::command` in `src/server/children.rs`), and gives every program the workspace's MCP address in `DECADE_MCP`, ending in `?workspace=<id>`. coax reads `DECADE_MCP` and passes it to its agent unchanged (`src/acp.rs` in coax).

## Proposal

- `Pane` gains `scratch: bool`, true for the workspace's scratch pane.
- A program started in a pane gets `DECADE_MCP` ending in `?workspace=<id>&pane=<name>`. A tool call to that address comes from that pane.
- `Pane` gains `you: bool`, true for the pane the call came from. Without `&pane=` it is false everywhere.
- Both fields are `#[serde(default)]`, so a reader built before them still parses the reply.
- `docs/protocol.md` describes both fields and the `pane` parameter of the address.

## Cost

`Pane` is public in `decade-channel`, so new fields break a caller that builds one with a struct literal. `decade-channel` moves its minor version. `decade` moves its minor for the protocol change.

## Open

- Whether the pane in the address goes stale when the pane is renamed (see the rename issue) or closed and its name reused.
